purpose: Sitagliptin is used to help control blood sugar levels in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is used along with a healthy diet and exercise to keep your blood sugar in a safe range. It is not used for type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis.
how_it_works: Your body naturally makes hormones after you eat that tell your pancreas to release insulin and lower the amount of sugar your liver makes. Sitagliptin works by blocking an enzyme that normally breaks down those helpful hormones, so they stick around longer and work better. This helps your body lower blood sugar in a more natural way, and importantly, it mainly works when your blood sugar is actually high, so it has a lower risk of causing dangerously low blood sugar on its own.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include stuffy or runny nose, sore throat, and upper respiratory infections like a cold. Some people may also experience headache, diarrhea, or stomach upset. These are usually mild and tend to go away on their own.
warnings: In rare cases, sitagliptin can cause a serious condition called pancreatitis, which is inflammation of the pancreas. Tell your doctor right away if you have severe stomach pain that does not go away, especially if it goes to your back. It has also rarely been linked to severe joint pain and a serious skin reaction called bullous pemphigoid. Let your doctor know about all your other medications, and always mention your kidney function, as the dose may need to be adjusted if your kidneys do not work well.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one 100 mg tablet taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. If you have kidney problems, your doctor may prescribe a lower dose of 50 mg or 25 mg once daily. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes and try to take it at the same time each day.
